messages:
alex: Quick q — streaming /v1/responses: are we standardizing on NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) or SSE? A few clients keep failing because they expect application/json and try to buffer the whole payload.
maria: We originally planned NDJSON for chunked responses — each chunk is a complete JSON object separated by \n. Server should set Content-Type: application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8 for streaming. Non-streaming stays application/json.
jon: Will changing the Content-Type break older SDKs that only look for application/json and do incremental parsing? Some JS clients call response.json() and explode.
alex: Also curious about structured outputs: for optional fields in the schema, should streaming chunks send null or omit the key entirely? Client parsing differs.
tara: My take: prefer explicit nulls for optional fields so the consumer knows the field shape. Omitting keys is ambiguous for typed clients. Avoid removing fields across versions.
maria: Proposed plan: 1) streaming -> application/x-ndjson; 2) add header X-Response-Format: ndjson;version=1 for explicit detection; 3) include schema_version in each object payload. This gives a clear signal for parsers.
jon: Suggestion: we should keep a compatibility mode. Maybe ?format=legacy wraps items into a top-level array (application/json). But thats memory-heavy and could OOM for long streams. Maybe only allow for short responses.
sam: For nullable vs empty string: we should document semantics: null == unknown/missing, empty string == known-empty. Server should not coerce empty->null automatically unless field flagged nullable in the schema.
alex: Example that broke a client: {"id":"abc","reason":""} vs {"id":"abc","reason":null}. The typed Go client expected *string and treated "" as a valid value, downstream logic misinterpreted.
maria: Implementation notes: runtime will 1) set Content-Type per response type, 2) add X-Response-Format header, 3) include schema_version in each object, 4) default to sending explicit nulls for optional fields unless configured. I'll open a PR with tests and sample client parsing snippets.
jon: Can we add a small compatibility shim in the SDKs to auto-detect NDJSON header and parse incrementally? That will reduce immediate breakage.
tara: Agreed. Also add an API lint that checks we don't drop fields in minor releases. Semver: changing required field presence is a major change.
alex: One more: for streaming errors mid-stream, do we send a final object {`{"__error": {"code":..., "message":...}}`} or close with an HTTP error? Clients differ.
maria: Plan: for stream, emit a terminal JSON chunk with `{"__error": {"code":..., "message":...}}` and then close the connection. Add docs for this pattern.
sam: I'll add sample Go/Python parsing snippets to the docs showing handling of null vs empty string and error terminal chunk.
alex: Ping @eng-runtime for review on the PR and the header choice — would prefer not to invent too many custom headers.
maria: tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform reviewers in the PR description. PR will also include changelog entry and a note for SDK teams.
ci-bot: Note: staging deploy queued for 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z if PR merges. :gear:
